general_information.Description: This course will prepare you for further study in higher level topics of 3D animation. In this course, you will learn all the tools to create your own animation and execute the entire visual production.
general_information.StudentTasks: Attendance: The course content and assigments are closely tied together; excessive absences will severely and negatively affect the learning process. Any student who misses 20% classes will fail the course. Assigments: You are given weekly assignments that are completed during the week. Assignments are evaluated against a set of technical criteria as well as on aesthetic quality. Assigments will account for 50 % of your grade. Late assignments will result in an automatic lowering of the grade. Attendance at each class and lab is expected. Missing classes or late arrival will result in a lowered grade. Final project: There will be an animated film, duration about 2 minutes, that will account for 50 % of your grade. The film will be determined and assigned at the end of this course. Plagiarism: is claiming the work someone else did, as work you did. DO NOT DO IT!!!! If you claim that you created the work someone else created, you will not pass the course.

schedule.Topic: An Overview of the Short Animation Process Creating a short animation from start to finish is a complicated, time-consuming task. It uses all of the skills you have developed while learning your way around your 3D software. As you work through the process, you will find that each step necessarily builds on everything that went before, and that to shortchange or entirely skip one of the steps will lead, surely, to disaster. Making a Short Animation consists of three stages: - Pre-production - Production - Post-production.

BlendShape and Facial Motion Control Animating facial expressions for characters is usually accomplished through the use of blend shapes. Although this is not the only way to animate expressions and speech, it is the most common because it is relatively straightforward to set up and animate. Learning Outcomes: In this section, you’ll learn how to: 1 - Create blend shape targets 2 - Paint blend shape weights 3 - Create a blend shape deformer 4 - Build a simple facial-animation rig.

Basic Animation Techniques For every animator there are a variety of techniques that are used throughout the animation process. This lesson contains a wide selection of very useful tools and techniques for animating. While creating a piece of animation, you may call upon some of these techniques dozens of times, others only once, but all of them will make a regular appearance in any animator's workflow. Learning Outcomes: This lesson covers basic animation techniques in Maya: 1 - Setting Key Frames 2 - Graph Editor 3 - Dopesheet Editor 4 - Animation Layers 5 - Editable Motion Trails 6 - Motion Path

The Twelve Basic Priciples of Animation (part 1) The purpose of animation is to serve the story e to capture images of life, and in the process communicate to others, even if it just means giving them a thrill ride. To this end, you need to make your animation believable. This doesn’t just mean realism. There are cues that pull people into the action. Animators at Walt Disney Studio wanted to create a kind of animation that felt real and let the audience respond to the character and story. As they observed and practiced what was at the time a new art, they developed a set of guidelines for animating. Two of these pioneers, Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston, set them out in 1981 in their book The Illusion of Life: Disney Animation. These guidelines have become standard for the animation industry. Learning Outcomes: In this lesson, you will learn: 1 - Squash and Stretch 2 - Anticipation 3 - Staging 4 - Straight-Ahead Action and Pose to Pose 5 - Follow Through and Overlapping Action 6 - Arcs

Cycles CYCLES, or animation meant to loop or repeat, are a mainstay of the animation industry. From games to film, to TV, cycles will most certainly be a part of your career in animation to a varied extent. The ability to quickly create realistic and appealing cycles is the hallmark of the experienced animator. Learning Outcomes: In this lesson , you'll learn how to: 1 - Create a basic cycle animation 2 - Walk cycle 3 - Flying Cycle 4 - Quad Cycle

schedule.Topic: Modeling and texturing Modeling and texturing are two of the primary jobs within the field of 3D animation and are closely tied to one another. Modeling is the act of creating a 3D object. Texturing is applying the color and surface properties to the model. Every industry that uses 3D animation must start with the creation of a model, which then serves as the foundation for all the other steps in the production pipeline. Texturing is the stage after a model is created, and the application of the texture depends on the geometry type used to create the model.

schedule.Topic: Rigging and Skinning Rigging and skinning is the art of adding controls to your characters so they can be posed and animated according to the needs of your project. The rigging/skinning combination is probably the most technically demanding, and is often the most frustrating step in the entire process of creating a short animation.
